title.value: Run an AI agent on a Nokia 110 feature phone

introduction.value: Author reverse-engineered a 48MB-RAM Nokia 110 to run an AI agent on it and automate a few actions.

method.value: The author studied the Nokia 110 4G firmware and boot process, then ran custom code in RAM through the Calculator entry point. They turned Calculator into a chat app that sends typed messages to the DeepSeek chat API and acts on tool calls. OpenAI Codex helped build it. Because of the 48MB memory limit, they wrote a minimal custom agent, used smaller builds, compressed the payload and reused buffers.

outcome.value: It works as a prototype. Over mobile data, unplugged, it can answer questions, check the battery, switch the torch on and off, start a call and set an alarm. It is not permanent.

notes.value: The code is loaded into RAM from a computer and is lost on restart or power-off, so it must be reloaded each time. The source code isn't published.

source_text.body:
Run an AI agent on a Nokia 110 feature phone
Author reverse-engineered a 48MB-RAM Nokia 110 to run an AI agent on it and automate a few actions.
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The author studied the Nokia 110 4G firmware and boot process, then ran custom code in RAM through the Calculator entry point. They turned Calculator into a chat app that sends typed messages to the DeepSeek chat API and acts on tool calls. OpenAI Codex helped build it. Because of the 48MB memory limit, they wrote a minimal custom agent, used smaller builds, compressed the payload and reused buffers.
How it went
It works as a prototype. Over mobile data, unplugged, it can answer questions, check the battery, switch the torch on and off, start a call and set an alarm. It is not permanent.
Worth knowing
The code is loaded into RAM from a computer and is lost on restart or power-off, so it must be reloaded each time. The source code isn't published.

Stop when I can press [a key or send a message] on the device and see the action happen, and tell me each step to run on my own hardware before you change anything.
